messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: Sev2 - GPU capacity exhaustion (us-west-2). Autoscaler reporting repeated scale failures; queue length rising. Link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/4973216540

sre-ash: seeing a huge backlog on infer-queue: avg inflight 4.2k, wait > 60s. Autoscaler hit `max_replicas=120` and then started returning 429s. Pod scheduling failures: 'Insufficient gpu' and 'MIG slot mismatch'.

ml-surgeon-kim: looks like fragmentation from recent MIG-resize rollout. Many nodes have leftover 1x16g slices while jobs ask for 2x8g. Binpacking can't place, leads to stranded GPUs.

ops-jorge: confirmed MIG mismatch spikes in the allocator metrics. Repack windows are delayed by cooldown. We also see throttling in allocator controller (rate limit errors).

sre-ash: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable emergency-burst pool (temp oversubscribe) 2) manual eviction+repack of stale MIG slices 3) fallback to smaller model variant for high-throughput customers. Doing (1) now.

oncall-tilly: I'm oncall and jumping in. ash — what's done so far?

sre-ash: enabled burst pool: `api.v1.pools.enable("burst-temp-usw2", capacity=8)` — burst nodes spinning up. Started targeted evictions on nodes with >70% stranded fraction using `tools/evict --threshold 0.7 --dry-run=false`.

ops-jorge: started a controlled repack on pool small-gpus to consolidate free MIG slices. Running repack in 5 node batches to avoid cascading evictions.

ml-surgeon-kim: can we force a temporary model fallback? For embeddings-heavy tenants we can route to quantized v2-small which fits current node sizes. That will reduce token-per-second cost but buy headroom.

pm-ryan: prioritize customers: Acme AI (high SLA), StudyQ (high embed volume), and BetaLabs (non-critical). Customer-success-lena will coordinate comms.

customer-success-lena: sending initial notice to Acme + StudyQ: "We're investigating increased request latency for embeddings and generation; mitigation in progress. Expect improvements within 30-45m." I'll CC infra status page.

sre-ash: checklist for handoff to tilly (concise):
- emergency-burst pool enabled (nodes coming up)
- manual evictions started on 12 nodes (evict logs in /var/log/evict-4973216540.log)
- repack jobs queued: repack-job-4973-1..3 running
- autoscaler config bumped: `max_replicas` -> 200 (temporary) — note: must revert post-incident
- routing rule created for embeddings -> v2-small for tenant ids [A-123,B-456]

oncall-tilly: taking over. My immediate tasks: monitor burst pool join, watch allocator errors, and continue controlled repack. Will throttle repack if request errors spike. Marking myself as responder.

sre-ash: added troubleshooting snippet in thread:``` 
# check scheduling failures
kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector type=Warning | grep "Insufficient GPU"
# list nodes with stranded fraction > 0.5 (internal script)
python tools/metrics_query.py --metric stranded_fraction --gt 0.5 --pool small-gpus
```

ops-jorge: observed 25% of nodes with mixed MIG shapes (1x16g + 2x8g). Repack target: convert small leftovers to consistent 2x8g where feasible. Might need brief node reboots for MIG apply. Scheduling those in waves.

ml-surgeon-kim: routing fallback engaged for Acme and StudyQ. Early results: embedding latency for StudyQ reduced from ~85s -> ~12s. Some quality delta but within acceptable thresholds per eval run (precision drop ~1.2%).

customer-success-lena: Acme replied "app errors reduced but still seeing ~15s spikes for bulk jobs". I'm escalating to their CTO; will provide timeline.

pm-ryan: please capture postmortem notes (owner: tilly). We need a timeline + root cause + mitigations & config changes: autoscaler limits, MIG rollout process, and a safer repack schedule.

oncall-tilly: ack. Creating incident ticket CIF-4973216540. Handoff summary posted to ops-runbook. Current status: burst nodes active, repack in progress (batch 2/5), routing fallbacks active. Queue length decreasing but still 2.1k. Continuing to watch.

sre-ash: note: we should add a guard in MIG rollout pipeline to prevent mixed-slice churn during peak traffic windows. Also consider per-pool `max_replicas` tie to recent 1h avg queue to prevent autoscaler cap hitting unexpectedly.

ops-jorge: ongoing: running `node-reboot-window --batch-size 3 --wait 180s` for nodes needing MIG apply. Expect small blips in placement but balanced by burst nodes.

customer-success-lena: I'll update affected customers with ETA 2h and offer priority support for any job retries.

pm-ryan: good. Once stabilized let's schedule a post-incident review with infra, ML, product and CS.

noncall-tilly: last check before brief pause: queue 1.4k, scheduling failures down 80%, repack batch 3/5 started. Will resume active monitoring in 15m and update thread. :white_check_mark:
